questions.question: Intermolecular forces are:
options: The covalent bonds inside a molecule
The attractions between separate molecules, much weaker than covalent bonds
The forces between protons and electrons

questions.question: When water boils, what is overcome?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen
The nuclear forces in the oxygen atom
The intermolecular forces between water molecules — the molecules themselves stay intact
Both the intermolecular forces and the covalent bonds

questions.question: Breaking INTRAmolecular bonds is:
options: A chemical change that destroys the substance

questions.question: A substance with very strong intermolecular forces will tend to have:
options: A low boiling point and fast evaporation
High melting and boiling points and slow evaporation

questions.question: London (induced dipole) forces arise because:
options: Moving electrons create fleeting temporary dipoles that induce dipoles in neighbours

questions.question: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine a liquid and iodine a solid because:
options: London forces strengthen as the molecules get larger with more electrons
The lighter halogens have stronger forces

questions.question: Hydrogen bonding can occur only when hydrogen is covalently bonded to:
Ranked from weakest to strongest, the forces are:

subtopics.title: Boiling Points, Vapour Pressure and the Water Anomaly

questions.question: Water (light) boils at 100 °C while hydrogen sulfide (heavier) boils at −60 °C because:
options: Water hydrogen-bonds and hydrogen sulfide cannot — force type beats molecular size

questions.question: A liquid with WEAK intermolecular forces has:
options: High vapour pressure, fast evaporation and a low boiling point
Low vapour pressure and slow evaporation

questions.question: Ice floats on water because:
options: Solids always float on their liquids
Hydrogen bonds lock ice into an open lattice that is less dense than liquid water

questions.question: Nail polish remover feels cold on the skin because:
options: It is stored below room temperature
Its weakly-gripped molecules evaporate rapidly, taking heat from the skin

subtopics.title: Dissolving, Ion-Dipole Forces and Like Dissolves Like

questions.question: When sodium chloride dissolves in water, the ions are pulled from the lattice by:
options: Ion-dipole attractions between the ions and the charged ends of water molecules
Hydrogen bonds between sodium and chloride

questions.question: Around a dissolved sodium ion, water molecules orient with:
options: Their negative oxygen corners facing the positive ion
Their hydrogen sides facing the positive ion
Their oxygen corners facing away from the ion

questions.question: Candle wax dissolves in petrol because:
options: Petrol breaks the wax's covalent bonds
Both are non-polar and interact through comparable London forces

questions.question: Wax will NOT dissolve in water because:
options: Water molecules grip each other with hydrogen bonds far stronger than anything they could form with the wax

subtopics.title: The Glue Between, Not the Glue Within

questions.question: In the brick wall picture, the bricks and mortar stand for:
options: Chemical bonds within molecules and the weaker forces between molecules

questions.question: Steam rising from boiling water consists of:
options: Intact water molecules that have escaped their neighbours

questions.question: Sanitiser dries within seconds while water lingers because:
options: Sanitiser molecules barely grip each other, while water clings to itself strongly
Water evaporates upward and sanitiser downward

questions.question: The "flicker" grade of stickiness corresponds to:
options: London forces from momentary shifts of the electron cloud

questions.question: Big non-polar molecules like candle wax can be solids because:
options: Many weak flickers across a large molecule add up to a real grip
Solids do not need intermolecular forces

questions.question: The hydrogen bond is best described as:
options: A true chemical bond within a molecule
A strong intermolecular force, about a tenth the strength of a covalent bond
A force found in all molecules

questions.question: Without hydrogen bonding, water at room temperature would be:

subtopics.title: Why Salt Disappears and Oil Refuses

questions.question: A dissolved ion travels through water surrounded by:
options: A shell of oriented water molecules — its hydration escort
Other ions of the same charge

questions.question: Oil floats on water rather than dissolving because:
options: Water would have to break its own hydrogen bonds for no comparable attraction in return

questions.question: Greasy stains that water cannot remove come out in dry-cleaning fluid because:
options: Grease reacts chemically with the fluid
Both grease and the fluid are non-polar — like dissolves like

questions.question: A full-marks explanation of any solubility observation must name:
options: The forces in the solute, in the solvent, and between them, and whether the exchange pays
The boiling points of both substances
